subtype: Approach: using an everyday example to understand fractions [Thinking]
passage: Note from the tutor, Saturday. Sumit stared at three-fourths in his book and said, "It's just two numbers stuck together." His mother came out of the kitchen with a roti, cut it into four equal parts, and put three on his plate. Sumit looked at his plate, and then at the single piece left on the tray. "So the top number is how many I have," he said slowly. "And the bottom is how many parts it was cut into." He drew four boxes in his notebook and shaded three. I said nothing. He explained it to me twice. Chaitanya, tutor

qa.q: How many parts of the roti did Sumit's mother put on his plate?
qa.a: She cut it into four equal parts and put three on his plate.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling before his mother brought the roti, and what changed?
qa.a: He was puzzled and cut off from the idea, since three-fourths seemed like two numbers stuck together. After he saw the food, he became interested and eager to explain.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sumit use to understand other fractions, and why?
qa.a: He could fold a paper into equal parts and shade some. Seeing the parts in something he can hold makes the number less abstract.

qa.q: How might Sumit's mother see what happened at the table?
qa.a: She may feel glad that a small thing from the kitchen made her son understand. She did not explain the number, only cut the roti.

grounding: A boy cannot follow three-fourths until a roti is cut into four parts and he is given three, so real food gives the number a meaning.

subtype: Approach: using an everyday example to understand fractions [Thinking]
passage:
Diary, Tuesday night
Fractions were a fog all week. Miss wrote 3/4 on the board and I only saw two numbers with a line. Tonight at dinner I told Ama I didn't get it. She took a hot roti, folded it, and tore it into four pieces on my plate. Then she took one back. "How much is left, Pema, my boy?" "Three pieces." "Out of?" "Four." And it clicked. Three out of four. The bottom number is how many pieces the roti was cut into, the top is how many I have! I ate my three-fourths very slowly. Tomorrow I'll tell Urmila, who sits next to me, because she was lost too.

qa.q: How many pieces did Ama tear the roti into?
How did Pema feel when it clicked?
qa.a: Pema felt delighted and relieved after a foggy week, finally seeing what the top and bottom numbers mean.

qa.q: What other everyday things could Pema use to practise fractions?
qa.a: Cutting a fruit or folding paper into equal parts; real objects give the numbers a meaning he can hold.

qa.q: How might Urmila benefit from Pema's discovery?
qa.a: Urmila was lost too, so hearing about the roti could help her understand fractions the same way.

grounding: Shows a boy who cannot follow three-fourths until his mother tears a roti into four and takes one away, giving the number a real meaning.

subtype: Approach: using an everyday example to understand fractions [Thinking]
passage: At noon Ujjwal sat by the chulha in the courtyard, his slate on his knees. 3/4 still made no sense. "It's just a three sitting on a four," he complained to Asif, who had come over to eat. Ujjwal's mother flipped a roti off the tawa, laid it on his plate, and pressed the edge of her hand across it twice, making four pieces. She slid one onto Asif's plate. "How many are yours now?" "Three." "Out of how many?" Ujjwal looked from the roti to his slate. "Four. So the four is the whole roti in pieces, and the three is what I've got." He wiped the slate and drew a circle cut into four, shading three.

qa.q: Where did Ujjwal sit with his slate?
qa.a: By the chulha in the courtyard.

qa.q: How was Ujjwal feeling about fractions before the roti?
qa.a: He was frustrated and confused, complaining that 3/4 was just a three sitting on a four.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do next to check he really understands?
qa.a: Try 2/4 or 1/4 with the roti pieces, or draw them on his slate; if he can explain each, the idea has stuck.

qa.q: What was lunch like for Asif?
qa.a: Asif got an extra piece of roti and watched the lesson happen on the plate, so Asif may have learned fractions too.

grounding: Illustrates a boy grasping three-fourths when his mother cuts a roti into four and leaves him three, linking the number to real food.
